pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 🌐 **Strand 3 — Communication Networks**
Sub-strand 1: Computer Networks

Networks have changed how we buy, sell, pay and learn. In this unit you will explore online business, Mobile Money, cards, QR payments and cryptocurrency, and you will judge the potential of e-learning.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **Content standard**
- **B9.3.1.1** Know the concept of computer networking for global communications.

> 🧭 **What you will be able to do**
- **B9.3.1.1.1** Discuss types of e-commerce and the cashless society (Bitcoin, transaction cards, QR code payment system).
- **B9.3.1.1.2** Justify e-learning potentials.

> 🗺️ **Lessons in this unit**
- 8.1 E-Commerce and the Cashless Society
- 8.2 Justifying the Potential of E-Learning

**Core competencies developed:** Digital Literacy (DL5.1, DL5.3), Communication and Collaboration (CC8.1, CC8.5).

pages.title: E-Commerce and the Cashless Society
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B9.3.1.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- explain e-commerce and its types;
- explore selling, buying and paying online;
- discuss Mobile Money, cards, QR payments and Bitcoin.
**Electronic commerce (e-commerce)** is the buying and selling of goods and services, and the transfer of money, over the Internet or other electronic networks.
| **Type** | **Meaning** | **Example** |
|---|---|---|
| B2C – Business to Consumer | A business sells directly to individuals | Buying a phone from an online shop such as Jumia; ordering food through a delivery app |
| B2B – Business to Business | Businesses trade with other businesses | A supermarket ordering stock online from a manufacturer |
| C2C – Consumer to Consumer | Individuals sell to each other through a platform | Selling a used bicycle on Jiji or Facebook Marketplace |
| C2B – Consumer to Business | Individuals sell services or products to businesses | A freelance graphic designer selling designs to a company online |
| G2C / B2G – Government | Government services and payments online | Paying for a passport or registering a business online; paying taxes on the GRA portal |
## Buying and selling online
> 🪜 **Step by step — Typical online purchase**
1. Search or browse the online store and compare prices and reviews.
2. Add items to the **cart (basket)**.
3. Create an account or check out as a guest; enter the delivery address.
4. Choose a payment method: **Mobile Money**, **card**, **bank transfer**, **QR code** or **pay on delivery**.
5. Confirm the order; receive an email/SMS confirmation and tracking information.
6. Receive the goods; check them and leave a review. Use the return policy if necessary.

pages.title: The cashless society
pages.body:
## The cashless society
A **cashless society** is one in which most payments are made electronically rather than with notes and coins.
| **Payment method** | **How it works** |
|---|---|
| Mobile Money (MoMo) | Money is stored in an e-wallet linked to a phone number (MTN MoMo, Telecel Cash, AT Money). Users send, receive, pay bills and buy airtime with a PIN via USSD codes or apps. Since 2018 Ghana’s **mobile money interoperability** lets users send money between different networks and bank accounts; **GhanaPay** (2022) is a bank-led mobile money service. |
| Transaction cards | **Debit cards** take money directly from your bank account; **credit cards** let you borrow up to a limit and pay later; **prepaid cards** are loaded in advance. Brands include **Visa**, **Mastercard** and Ghana’s **gh-link**. Cards use a magnetic stripe, an EMV chip, or contactless (tap) technology. |
| QR code payment | A merchant displays a **QR code**; the customer scans it with a banking or MoMo app and authorises payment. Ghana’s **universal QR code (GhQR)**, introduced by the Bank of Ghana and GhIPSS in 2020, lets customers of different banks and wallets pay the same merchant code. |
| Online banking | Banks’ websites and apps for transfers, statements and bill payments |
| Cryptocurrency (e.g. Bitcoin) | **Bitcoin**, created in **2009** by a person or group using the name **Satoshi Nakamoto**, is a **digital currency** not issued by any central bank. Transactions are recorded on a public, shared ledger called a **blockchain**. Its value goes up and down sharply (it is **volatile**). |

> 🇬🇭 **Ghana connection — Cryptocurrency and the law in Ghana** In **December 2025** Ghana’s Parliament passed the **Virtual Asset Service Providers Bill**, giving the **Bank of Ghana** (and the Securities and Exchange Commission for some activities) power to license and supervise crypto exchanges and wallet providers. This makes crypto trading legal under regulation, but it does **not** make Bitcoin legal tender: the **Ghana cedi** remains Ghana’s official currency. Many crypto “investment” offers are scams, so be very careful.
| **Advantages of a cashless society** | **Disadvantages and risks** |
|---|---|
| Convenient, fast payments at any time | Fraud, scams and SIM-swap theft |
| Safer than carrying cash | Excludes people without phones, ID or network coverage |
| Records of transactions; easier budgeting | Transaction fees and taxes |
| Reduces cost of printing money; helps tax collection | System outages stop payments |
| Supports e-commerce and small businesses | Privacy: transactions can be tracked |
> 🛡️ **Safety first — Protect your money**
- Never share your **PIN** or **OTP**, even with someone claiming to be from your network or bank.
- Check the **name** shown before confirming any payment.
- Do not reverse “mistaken” transfers: report to your provider.
- Use only trusted, licensed shops and apps.

pages.title: The cashless society (continued)
pages.body:
> 🧪 **Activity — Online business plan**
In groups, design a small online business (e.g. selling school uniforms or local crafts). Decide the e-commerce type, platform (WhatsApp Business, Instagram, a website), payment methods (MoMo, QR, card), delivery method and how you will build customers’ trust. Present your plan.

pages.title: Justifying the Potential of E-Learning
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B9.3.1.1.2
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- explain e-learning, its benefits and disadvantages;
- discuss collaborative platforms.
**E-learning** (electronic learning) is learning delivered through digital technology: online courses, video lessons, virtual classrooms, educational apps, e-books and learning management systems. It may be **synchronous** (live, at the same time, e.g. a Zoom class) or **asynchronous** (self-paced, e.g. recorded videos).
| **Benefits** | **Disadvantages** |
|---|---|
| Learn anytime, anywhere, at your own pace | Needs devices, electricity and Internet data |
| Access to expert teachers and rich resources (videos, simulations) | Less face-to-face interaction; some learners feel isolated |
| Learning continues during closures (e.g. COVID-19 in 2020) | Requires self-discipline; easy to get distracted |
| Lower cost for travel and printed materials | Practical skills can be hard to teach online |
| Instant feedback through online quizzes | Cheating and plagiarism are harder to control |

pages.title: Collaborative platforms
pages.body:
## Collaborative platforms
| **Platform** | **How it supports collaboration** |
|---|---|
| iBox (Ghana) | An **offline** learning management server developed by **CENDLOS** (Centre for National Distance Learning and Open Schooling). Learners connect over the school’s local network to curriculum-aligned lessons and resources without needing the Internet. |
| Ad hoc network | Devices connect directly to each other (e.g. a laptop hotspot or Wi-Fi Direct) without a router, so a group can share files and a single Internet connection |
| Wikis | Websites that groups edit together (e.g. a class wiki of revision notes) |
| Google Docs / Microsoft 365 | Several learners edit the same document at the same time, with comments and version history |
| Google Classroom, Microsoft Teams | Class discussions, assignment submission, feedback |
> 🧪 **Activity — Debate and justify**
Debate: “E-learning can replace classroom teaching in Ghanaian JHSs.” Then, as a group, write a short paragraph justifying how e-learning can best **support** classroom teaching in your school.

pages.body:
> ✏️ **Review exercises** — answer these in your exercise book or on the computer, then check with your teacher.
## Short answer questions
1. Explain **four** types of e-commerce with examples.
2. Describe how a QR code payment is made.
3. What is Bitcoin? State **two** risks of cryptocurrency.
4. Justify **four** potentials of e-learning in Ghana.
5. Explain how Google Docs supports collaborative projects.
